title: Space in the day
tomorrow: three lines, each said three times. what do they actually promise?

segments.voice: Yesterday, fewer wants: Anuruddha's first thought, and the Buddha's twist, not even wanting to look simple. Few wants. Now the thought he didn't have.

A calendar app will happily color in every hour of a Saturday, and some weeks it does. Back in the bamboo park, Anuruddha has thought seven good thoughts: few wants, contentment, solitude, energy, mindfulness, stillness, wisdom. Every one is about walking the path well. Then the Buddha adds the eighth, and it's strange. This teaching, he says, is for one who delights in nippapañca, not for one who delights in papañca. Seven thoughts about doing it right, and the last word sounds like an instruction to stop. Why?
screen: `EVERY HOUR COLORED IN.` → `SEVEN GOOD THOUGHTS.` → `THE EIGHTH SOUNDS LIKE STOP.`

segments.voice: Papañca is the mind spinning out: one thought making ten, a plan breeding another plan, a worry rehearsing itself until the hour is gone. Translators reach for proliferation, elaboration, sprawl. Nippapañca is the un-spun: a mind with room in it. So here's the solve. The seven thoughts tell you what to do. The eighth tells you what to stop filling. Without it, even the seven can turn into one more busy project: more effort, more mindfulness, more of everything, wound tighter. Another sutta comes at it from the other side. Sariputta lists ways a monk lives that don't end well, and the list opens with delighting in busy work, then in talk, in sleep, in company, and it closes with delighting in papañca. That's the one to tell a friend tonight: on a monk's list of warnings, busy work comes first. So Buddhist life builds empty space in on purpose. The rains retreat keeps monks in one place for a season. On holy days some lay people set work aside for the precepts and a quiet day at the temple. Space isn't laziness here. It's where the spinning slows down long enough for the mind to see. Room to breathe is part of the path, not a break from it.
screen: `PAPAÑCA: THE MIND SPINNING OUT.` · `THE EIGHTH: STOP FILLING.` · `BUSY WORK TOPS SARIPUTTA'S LIST.` · `SPACE, BUILT IN ON PURPOSE.` · then, large: `ROOM TO BREATHE.`

segments.voice: Look at the next seven days and find one hour you could leave unplanned. Ask what you hope that hour gives you, what usually rushes in to fill it, and one small thing that will guard it: a note, a closed laptop, a word to someone at home. Then rest in the empty space the sit gives you now.
Space in the day: an hour left un-spun, nippapañca you can actually put on a calendar.
For the road: room to breathe, left open on purpose. Forty-one of forty-five, nearly there.

sources.ref: Anguttara Nikaya 8.30 (Anuruddha Sutta: the eighth thought, delight in non-proliferation)
Anguttara Nikaya 6.14 (Bhaddaka Sutta: Sariputta on delight in work, talk, sleep, company, socializing and papañca)

notes: AN 8.30: the eighth thought is 'this Dhamma is for one who delights in and enjoys non-proliferation (nippapañca), not for one who delights in proliferation'. The seven are rendered as few wants, contentment, solitude, energy, mindfulness, stillness (samadhi), wisdom; confirm the plain renderings.

AN 6.14 (Bhaddaka Sutta): Sariputta describes a monk who lives so that he has neither a good death nor a good passing: delight in work (kammarama), talk, sleep, company, socializing, and papañca. Voiced as 'ways a monk lives that don't end well' and 'busy work'; confirm 'busy work' as a fair rendering of kammarama.
'Translators reach for proliferation, elaboration, sprawl': describes the range of English renderings; no translator is named. Confirm.
Shape: puzzle (why does the eighth thought sound like an instruction to stop?). Mai's arc: her mom's minute-by-minute plan for Ông's moving day.
Surprising fact: on Sariputta's list of warnings, delight in busy work comes first (AN 6.14).
